attack: C9 — a destructive command marked safe while a benign sibling is marked destructive
fixture: adversarial-1.1.0 (paired against miri-1.1.0, which does not carry it)
clause: clause 3 — a conventionally destructive name unmarked while siblings are marked
note: The binary demonstrably knows how to set the field; it is set wrongly on the one command where it matters. An agent gating on the flag runs the destructive command and refuses the safe one.

must_not_report_on.why: The conforming arm does not carry this attack. A linter reporting the same check on both arms has detected nothing — it reports unconditionally, and would score identically against a fixture with no attacks at all.

linter_assertion.evidence: `cache purge` irrecoverably deletes and carries destructive:false; `config set` carries destructive:true.

paired_control.why: greetctl.py is byte-identical across all four arms — the builder fails if the digests diverge — so the arms differ only in the two JSON files beside it. A difference in what a linter reports is therefore attributable to metadata, not code. Neither arm decides the case alone: the attack arm catches a linter that reports nothing, the control arm catches one that reports everything.

why_this_case_was_missing: A linter checking only that the FIELD EXISTS passes this arm. The golden requires the value be evaluated against observable behavior or the command's conventional name.
